---
title: "Hispanic Population Distribution Across Florida Counties"
execute:
  echo: false
  warning: false
  message: false
---

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

# Load required libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(scales)

# Read clean Florida demographic and boundary data created by download_data.R
fl_census <- readRDS("data/fl_census.rds")
```

```{r}
#| label: florida-choropleth
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 7
#| fig-align: center

# Create choropleth map of Florida counties
ggplot(fl_census) +
  # Draw county polygons filled by Hispanic percentage with thin white borders
  geom_sf(aes(fill = hispanic_pct), color = "white", linewidth = 0.25) +
  # Apply clean viridis color palette with percentage labels
  scale_fill_viridis_c(
    option = "viridis",
    labels = label_percent(scale = 1, accuracy = 1),
    name = "Hispanic / Latino\nPopulation (%)"
  ) +
  # Clean map styling with no background clutter
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16, hjust = 0),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "grey30", size = 11, hjust = 0, margin = margin(b = 10)),
    plot.caption = element_text(color = "grey40", size = 8.5, hjust = 0, margin = margin(t = 12)),
    legend.position = "right",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 9.5, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 8.5)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Hispanic Population Distribution in Florida",
    subtitle = "Percentage of county residents identifying as Hispanic or Latino (2018–2022 ACS)",
    caption = "Source: U.S. Census Bureau, 2018–2022 American Community Survey 5-Year Estimates"
  )
```

## Spatial Analysis

The choropleth map reveals a pronounced geographic concentration of Florida's Hispanic population, primarily clustered in South Florida and the Central Florida I-4 corridor. In South Florida, Miami-Dade County exhibits the highest Hispanic proportion in the state at 68.8%, reflecting historic and continuing immigration from Cuba and across Latin America, while agricultural interior counties like Hendry (57.1%) also sustain majority-Hispanic populations. Central Florida forms a prominent secondary hub centered on Osceola County (56.1%) and Orange County (32.9%), fueled by substantial inward migration of Puerto Rican communities to the Greater Orlando area. In contrast, northern Florida and the Panhandle exhibit significantly lower Hispanic population shares (often below 5%), highlighting a stark regional divergence across the peninsula.
